title: Prove sharp unsigned convolution carry capacity (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped proof with finite corroboration: for unsigned base-B convolution of an a-digit and b-digit input, with B>=2 and zero initial carry, the exact uniform carry capacity is min(a,b)(B-1)-1. A closed form gives every positionwise maximum, and the all-maximal digit pair attains them simultaneously.

```diff
- Square-input sufficient carry cap: q(B-1), PR3787 / PR3808
+ Sharp cap: q(B-1)-1
+ Rectangular cap: min(a,b)(B-1)-1
```

A conventional binary carry field saves one value bit when q(B-1) is a power of two. This is an exact numeric range result, without a physical implementation saving or new kappa. Only research/rectangular-convolution-carry is added.

The contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Jose Manuel / jmbarrancoml's PR3787 for the fixed-tape FFT/radix interface, James Reed / jwr404's PR3808 for the sufficient carry range and recovery evidence, and their retained FFT/Karatsuba/Gaussian/fixed-tape lineage. Predecessor results are cited, not audited or replayed. Radix convolution and the proof methods are classical; no literature-priority claim is made.

## Evidence

- Before: the cited square-input interface supplies the sufficient q(B-1) cap.
- After: PROOF.md proves the sharp positionwise envelope for every integer B>=2 and a,b>=1. The standalone checker attains every predicted position maximum on 79,541 input pairs in 86 domains, checking 583,845 carry positions.
- Another 31,744 maximal-digit profiles check 1,079,296 positions; 2,016 coefficients agree with literal convolution. There are 4,032 numeric-capacity cases, fourteen rejecting controls and three scope boundaries.
- On macOS arm64, CPython 3.12.15, the registered warning-strict normal and optimized checks take 1.295 and 1.316 seconds. Their generated file-hash-bound receipts are identical. These timings establish the replay budget, not a speedup.
- Metadata, exact committed bytes and source-history ancestry pass at 77ac6bd8dd9ea2db9024351956edec3f7152d9b1. Official export integrity and declared-input coverage pass. Normal/optimized Git-free read-only replays agree with the local receipt; all seven exported files remain unchanged. Three deliberate semantic mutations reject under optimized Python.

Exact reproduction commands, from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/rectangular-convolution-carry/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -O -B research/rectangular-convolution-carry/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/rectangular-convolution-carry
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/rectangular-convolution-carry --check-source-history
```

Substitute another CPython 3.12 path on another machine. Expected markers are PASS_RECTANGULAR_CONVOLUTION_CARRY, PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE and PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES. The checker needs only the standard library and writes nothing.

## Limitations

The theorem requires ordinary unsigned radix convolution and zero initial carry. Signed digits, restricted leading-digit ranges, arbitrary coefficient streams and rounded coefficient acquisition are outside scope. Encoded allocation, local-total width, conversion, cleanup and full caller costs remain unproved here. No physical backend, predecessor scientific replay, selected cold replay, Lean or Docker check was run. The selected PR6030 frontier and all five framework assumptions are unchanged. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

1. Can an actual encoded carry field use the smaller range without extra conversion or cleanup? Start with the carry-field and local-total allocations of one physical-fft-word call; a complete charged implementation is missing.
2. What is the sharp envelope when the leading radix digits have smaller bounds? Start with those two restricted maximal digits; the changed domain is not covered here.

## Related open work

- [PR6255](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6255) removes horizontal padding in carry-graded box convolution. Its carries describe mixed-radix coordinate-index overflow; this proof bounds unsigned coefficient-digit normalization carries. Neither result computes the other's carry-capacity quantity, so no numerical agreement or disagreement is inferred.
- [PR956](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/956) studies an exact scalar/index RAM Gaussian and convolution provider. It supplies a different implementation/model obligation; no carry-capacity number is compared or recomputed here.

Completion-time searches and this account's open PRs created since the advance CLAIM were refreshed. No other open PR studying this unsigned convolution carry capacity was identified in that coverage. PR3787 and PR3808 are merged predecessors.

## CI notes

Both hosted checks, `plan` and `replay (research/rectangular-convolution-carry)`, passed at commit `77ac6bd8dd9ea2db9024351956edec3f7152d9b1` in [run 41048227446](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41048227446). The completed checks were read once; run metadata confirms that exact head and successful conclusion. Both registered checks and all required package/source-history checks also passed locally. Hosted replay certifies the registered finite checks; the universal theorem rests on PROOF.md, without independent human or formal proof-kernel acceptance.

## Merge Danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: package. This adds an isolated proof and read-only checker; shared code, frozen evidence and selected records are unchanged.
